pairs.evidence: src-tauri/src/commands/recipes/recipe_adoption.rs:84 the adoption gate is well built but bound to no door: it is registered (src-tauri/src/ipc_shards/shard_2.rs:206) and no frontend code invokes it, while UI adoption writes the use case directly via src/features/templates/sub_recipes/libs/useAdoption.ts:62 - the gate refuses nothing a user does

techniques.evidence: src-tauri/src/commands/recipes/recipe_adoption.rs:105 requirements the gate could not verify fail closed with a named reason instead of scoring Eligible
src-tauri/src/commands/recipes/recipe_adoption.rs:370 seeded known-bad input (corrupt tool requirements) asserted to refuse; siblings at :291, :319, :419 prove the other refusal branches red

src/lib/commandNames.generated.ts:25 adopt_recipe_for_persona exists only as a generated name; the action that adopts (useAdoption.ts:62 mutateUseCases) never reaches it, so the refusal is blocking by construction and advisory by wiring

src/features/templates/sub_recipes/libs/useAdoption.ts:62 the underlying capability (appending a recipe use case to design_context) is not confined to the gated wrapper; nothing proves adoption routes through recipe_adoption.rs

pairs.registryProposal: enforcement-binding is written for the CI-pipeline to merge-decision join; this case is the same failure inside an app: a correct, tested refusal command registered over IPC while the user-facing action writes through a different door. Worth an application or a use_when trigger ("a gate command with no caller on the action path").
